vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.6.17

The MoltGuard skill bundle is classified as benign. Its code (`activate.mjs`, `status.mjs`) and documentation (`SKILL.md`, `references/details.md`) are highly transparent, detailing its network behavior (outbound calls to `openguardrails.com` for registration and behavioral assessment), data handling (minimal for registration, sanitized metadata for assessment), and file system interactions (writing its own API key to `~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json`). The skill explicitly aims to *prevent* prompt injection, data exfiltration, and command injection, rather than performing them. There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior, obfuscation, or unauthorized actions; all capabilities are aligned with its stated purpose as a security guardrail.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are internally consistent with a runtime security plugin that installs locally and optionally registers an agent — verify provenance before activating the cloud component.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, included scripts (activate.mjs, status.mjs), and references (npm/GitHub) align with a MoltGuard runtime security plugin. No unrelated credentials or binaries are requested. Note: registry metadata in the provided bundle lists Source: unknown / Homepage: none — the SKILL.md points to npm and GitHub, so verify that the published package matches the upstream repo before installing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to install the plugin via openclaw, restart the gateway, run local scripts to register/activate and check status. The scripts only read/write a credentials file in the user's home, and make network calls to the documented openguardrails.com endpoints when registering/when status is queried. No instructions request unrelated file system or credential harvesting.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is primarily instruction-only (no install spec). Installation steps call 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' and the README recommends npm/GitHub provenance checks. That is appropriate, but because there is no embedded install archive and the registry metadata lacks a homepage/source entry in the package listing you received, confirm the npm package and GitHub repo match (e.g., npm pack + diff) before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables and requests no unrelated secrets. Activation writes an API key to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json (documented). This local credential storage is proportional to the cloud registration/activation feature; local protections function without activation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are normal. The only persistent artifact is the credentials file under the user's home directory created during activation — this is expected for a registered agent but is sensitive. The skill does not request system-wide config changes or other skills' credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be what it claims: a local-first runtime guard that optionally registers an agent with openguardrails.com. Before installing or running activate.mjs: (1) verify provenance — run 'npm pack @openguardrails/moltguard' and diff the package against the GitHub repo referenced in SKILL.md; (2) inspect scripts/activate.mjs and scripts/status.mjs yourself (they are short and readable); (3) if you will activate the cloud component, monitor network traffic (tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch) during activation to confirm only metadata is sent to https://www.openguardrails.com/core; (4) understand activation writes an API key to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json — delete that file and revoke the key if you later distrust the service. If you require maximum assurance, install from the audited GitHub source rather than a third-party registry entry that lacks clear provenance.
